title: [2611.19970] Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
note: Abstract page, v1 of 15 Nov 2026, the only version; one author (Ali Nikseresht); eess.SY, stat.AP, stat.ME; arXiv non-exclusive licence. Day-ahead load model: fractional temperature kernel for building thermal inertia, breaks and long memory estimated jointly, reserves from the joint hourly error law. Headline: MAPE 15.7% and 10.3% below the best of ten benchmarks. No code link on the page.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (full text)
note: Benchmarks: vanilla and recency MLR, Kalman-filtered adaptive GAM, APLF, GBDT with and without load lags, MLP, LSTM, patch transformer, KAN. All re-implemented by the author, stated to use the same information set and yearly retraining; hyperparameters are listed in the supplement. Year table: proposed is lowest in all 9 ISO-NE years and PJM 2020, 2021; LSTM is lower in PJM 2019 (2.18 vs 2.26%).

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (full text)
note: Ablation (all PJM test years; ISO-NE on 2009, 2012, 2014, 2016 only, hence full model 1.53% there, not 1.56%). MAPE rises without the residual model by 54.6 / 64.1%, without the boosted correction 67.9 / 24.3%, without thermal memory 37.0 / 28.6%. Swapping the fractional kernel for an exponential one costs only 3.1 / 1.2% (PJM 2.13 to 2.16%). Online detector: no accuracy change.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (full text)
note: Other results. Eight GEFCom2017 ISO-NE zones, 2016, zonal temperatures: mean MAPE 2.30% against 4.95% for the author's rerun of adaptive multitask learning under the same day-ahead protocol. Reserve schedule for a pumped-storage plant: storage energy limit breached on 4.1 and 8.5% of days, against 36.7 and 57.5% when error correlations are ignored. Heating kernel order 0.57 (ISO-NE), 0.45 (PJM).

title: Research task (standard): primary sources for or against arXiv 2611.19970
note: One research task, LinkedIn excluded. Sources: the arXiv abstract, HTML and PDF, two earlier papers by the author, two GitHub account listings. It named no code repository, data release, pre-registration, replication, critique or citing work; nothing contradicts the paper. Its remark that 1.56 and 1.53% MAPE are inconsistent is wrong: the ablation covers four ISO-NE years only.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (full text)
note: Setup. Issued 10:00 on day D-1 for the 24 hourly loads of day D (leads 15 to 38 h). Day-D temperatures are taken as observed. Yearly re-estimation. ISO-NE system load Mar 2003 to Apr 2017 (GEFCom2017 files), test 2008-2016, 3288 days. PJM footprint load Jan 2017 to Nov 2021 (Ruan et al. open data, 3 airport stations), test 2019-2021, 1065 days.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (full text)
note: Table III. Proposed MAPE 1.56% ISO-NE, 2.13% PJM; RMSE 0.338, 2.65 GW. Best benchmarks: LSTM 1.85%, GBDT with load lags 2.38%; text says 15.7% and 10.3% lower. Vanilla MLR 3.52 / 4.45%, recency MLR 2.89 / 3.64%. Pinball loss 6.8 and 9.1% below the best probabilistic benchmark; 90% intervals cover 91.9 and 91.6%. Diebold-Mariano: better than all ten at 5% in both systems.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (full text)
note: Method and release. Mean: regression on calendar terms and fractionally filtered heating and cooling degree-hours, plus a LightGBM correction; residual: multiscale fractional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck conditioned on recent errors. 3 to 4 CPU minutes per test year. No code or data availability statement, no repository link, no pre-registration. Stated limit: temperatures are observed.
